comparison: Both evaluate EpiSC differentiation capacity (C33-C34, C157-C164, C183-C185). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with microarray data providing mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether 'micropattern culture has not fully revealed the spectrum of EpiSC differentiation' and challenging the 'functionally restricted' conclusion.

Both evaluate BMP signaling patterns (C128-C137). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with pSMAD1/5/8 data demonstrating spatial gradients matching in vivo patterns. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting that direct signaling activity measurements are more mechanistic than marker expression alone.

Both evaluate diameter-dependent patterning (C119-C127). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes morphological confounds in smaller colonies. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without specific concerns, as findings parallel established human ESC work.

Both discuss system symmetry and lack of extraembryonic tissues (C174-C178). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as valid characterization of system properties. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED but request clarification on how radial symmetry differs from other 3D systems that generate asymmetry.

Both evaluate CHIR experiment on receptor-mediated patterning (C139-C142). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes mechanism remains inferential. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, consistent with prior human micropattern work on endogenous inhibitors.

Both evaluate spatial patterning in flat-disc geometry (C32, C38-C39, C165-C172, C188). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about strength of parallel to in vivo development, requesting better articulation of system uniqueness.

Both evaluate endogenous WNT role and marker patterns (C57-C67). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear XAV939 experiment results. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about spatial marker documentation, asking about SOX2 and NANOG staining at different stages.

Both evaluate EMT processes (C5-C6, C31, C100-C116). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with cadherin switching and ACTIVIN inhibition experiments demonstrating SMAD2/3 requirement. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting that common pathways regulate in vitro and in vivo systems.

Both evaluate mesoderm subtype identification (C83-C93). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple marker coexpression patterns matching in vivo signatures. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, specifically questioning Mesoderm 1 identification based on GATA6/OTX2 which are also expressed in endoderm.

Both evaluate micropattern system development and marker validation (C30, C47-C51, C56). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate pluripotency and lineage markers. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting 'not easy to assess fidelity...on basis of a few markers' and requesting better organization of marker data.

Both discuss implications for human studies (C186). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as proposed future work rather than completed findings. Peer reviewers find SUPPORTED as reasonable suggestion for future work without critique.

Both evaluate BMP removal switching to anterior fates (C7, C37, C143-C156, C180-C181). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes ambiguity in anterior PS versus AxM distinction. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about marker validation, noting general concerns about whether 2-3 markers uniquely identify cell types.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about speculative assignments ('may correspond to'), consistent with concerns about overstating certainty.

Both acknowledge uncertainty about embryonic versus extraembryonic mesoderm distinction (C169-C170). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriately acknowledged limitation. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting this as acknowledged uncertainty rather than definitive claim.
